final_proof:
Let
\[
\operatorname{Log}a=\{v\in\mathbb C:e^v=a\}
\]
denote the multivalued complex logarithm (so \(\operatorname{Log}0=\varnothing\)), and let
\[
\operatorname{Arg}a=\{\theta\in\mathbb R:a=|a|e^{i\theta}\}.
\]
In particular, \(\operatorname{Arg}0=\mathbb R\). As usual for expressions containing multifunctions, the right-hand side in Definition 2 means the union over all choices of the displayed argument and all values of the displayed logarithm. Thus, with \(q=z^2+1\), that right-hand side is
\[
B(z)=\left\{\ell+2k\pi i:\begin{array}{l}
k\in\mathbb Z,\ \theta\in\operatorname{Arg}q,\\[2pt]
\ell\in\operatorname{Log}\!\left(z+\sqrt{|q|}\,e^{i\theta/2}\right)
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
We prove that
\[
B(z)=\{w\in\mathbb C:\sinh w=z\}.
\]

First note that, as \(\theta\) ranges over \(\operatorname{Arg}q\), the numbers
\[
r=\sqrt{|q|}\,e^{i\theta/2}
\]
are exactly the square roots of \(q\). Indeed, if \(\theta\in\operatorname{Arg}q\), then
\[
r^2=|q|e^{i\theta}=q.
\]
Conversely, suppose \(r^2=q\). If \(q\ne0\), choose \(\phi\in\mathbb R\) with \(r=|r|e^{i\phi}\). Then \(|r|=\sqrt{|q|}\), and \(2\phi\in\operatorname{Arg}q\), so \(r=\sqrt{|q|}e^{i(2\phi)/2}\). If \(q=0\), then \(r=0\); since \(\sqrt{|q|}=0\) and \(\operatorname{Arg}0=\mathbb R\), the same displayed form again represents \(r\). This also covers the branch points \(z=\pm i\).

Now take \(w\in\mathbb C\) with \(\sinh w=z\), and put \(u=e^w\). Since \(u\ne0\), the identity \(\sinh w=(e^w-e^{-w})/2\) gives
\[
u-u^{-1}=2z,
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
u^2-2zu-1=0.
\]
Consequently
\[
(u-z)^2=z^2+1=q.
\]
By the preceding square-root observation there is a \(\theta\in\operatorname{Arg}q\) such that \(u-z=\sqrt{|q|}e^{i\theta/2}\). Therefore
\[
e^w=u=z+\sqrt{|q|}e^{i\theta/2},
\]
which says that \(w\) is one of the values of the logarithm in the definition of \(B(z)\). Taking \(k=0\), we conclude that \(w\in B(z)\).

Conversely, take \(w\in B(z)\). Then for some \(k\in\mathbb Z\), some \(\theta\in\operatorname{Arg}q\), and some \(\ell\in\operatorname{Log}(z+\sqrt{|q|}e^{i\theta/2})\), we have
\[
w=\ell+2k\pi i.
\]
Set \(r=\sqrt{|q|}e^{i\theta/2}\) and \(u=z+r\). We have \(r^2=q=z^2+1\), and hence
\[
u^2-2zu-1=(z+r)^2-2z(z+r)-1=r^2-z^2-1=0.
\]
This equation also shows that \(u\ne0\). Because \(e^\ell=u\) and \(e^{2k\pi i}=1\), we have \(e^w=u\). Dividing the quadratic equation by \(u\) now yields \(u-u^{-1}=2z\). Therefore
\[
\sinh w=\frac{e^w-e^{-w}}2=\frac{u-u^{-1}}2=z.
\]
Thus \(B(z)\subseteq\{w:\sinh w=z\}\), and the reverse inclusion was proved above. The two multifunction definitions are therefore equivalent for every \(z\in\mathbb C\).
